sources.label: Design Ontology Harness
sources.notes: Baseline interaction candidates authored in this repository. They exist so every axis has more than one defensible answer; a pool of one is not a choice.

patterns.label: Immediate content swap
patterns.rationale: Dense operational surfaces read faster when new content simply appears; motion costs attention the operator needs elsewhere.
guardrails: Preferred when the user is scanning or comparing many rows at once.
Never animate position; only the content itself changes.
Keep a visible non-motion cue for what changed.

patterns.label: Staged list entry
patterns.rationale: A short stagger communicates that several items arrived together without implying they are ranked.
guardrails: Cap the stagger so the last item is not perceptibly late.
Never stagger more than one screen of items.
Drop to a single opacity change when reduced motion is requested.

patterns.label: In-place detail expansion
patterns.rationale: Expanding where the user already looks keeps the origin of the detail obvious and avoids a context jump.
guardrails: The trigger must stay visible while the detail is open.
Animate opacity and transform, never surrounding layout geometry.
Preserve scroll position of the surrounding surface.

patterns.label: Typographic weight emphasis
patterns.rationale: Editorial surfaces carry emphasis through type weight and contrast, so selection reads without adding a coloured frame.
guardrails: Do not rely on weight alone where the state is critical; pair with a non-typographic cue.
Keep the layout stable — reserve the heavier metrics so nothing reflows.
Focus visibility stays independent of this emphasis.

patterns.label: Surface elevation emphasis
patterns.rationale: A small elevation change separates the chosen surface from its peers without recolouring it.
guardrails: Elevation must map to a token, never an ad-hoc shadow.
Only one surface may be lifted within a group at a time.
Do not combine with an animated border on the same element.

patterns.label: Determinate progress
patterns.rationale: When the remaining work is measurable, showing the measurement beats showing activity.
guardrails: Use only when real progress is known; never fake the fill rate.
Pair the bar with a numeric or textual status.
Fall back to an indeterminate pattern rather than inventing a percentage.

patterns.label: Structural skeleton
patterns.rationale: Reserving the shape of the incoming content prevents the layout shift that a centred spinner invites.
guardrails: The skeleton must match the real content's geometry, not a generic grey block.
Expose an accessible loading status; the shimmer is not an announcement.
Hold the shimmer to the loop budget and stop it as soon as content lands.

patterns.label: Context crossfade
patterns.rationale: A brief crossfade marks that the frame of reference changed while the surrounding chrome stayed put.
guardrails: Chrome and navigation must not move during the fade.
Do not crossfade when the underlying data is identical.
Keep the outgoing and incoming content from overlapping legibly.

patterns.label: Anchored positional shift
patterns.rationale: Moving a single shared anchor between positions explains the relationship between two views better than fading both.
guardrails: Exactly one anchor element may move per transition.
The anchor must exist in both the outgoing and incoming state.
Snap the anchor into place immediately under reduced motion.

rules.label: Reduced motion fallback
rules.statement: Every non-essential motion pattern must define a static, opacity-only, or skipped reduced-motion behavior.

rules.label: Reference does not override product truth
rules.statement: Candidates inform morphology and affordance, but product brief, semantic tokens, component contracts, accessibility, and implementation rules remain authoritative.

rules.label: One primary motion per surface
rules.statement: A screen carries one primary movement plus subordinate micro-response. Equal motion on every element is the signature of a generated layout, not a designed one.
